content_md:
Just want to note that Tyler Cowen has admitted that he's never experienced out of control laughter. I don't know why he thinks he's the right person to weigh in here.

On the most famous comedy sketch ever, "Who's On First?"

> Well, no, it is not funny, it would be too easy to relieve the dramatic tension by having Abbott explain the actual situation to Costello. One is not wrong to call the whole thing stupid. Yet there is another reading of the skit which stands at least some chance of being funny, though it is not funny either.[—marginalrevolution.com](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2026/10/is-whos-on-first-funny.html)

There's a couple other problems with this analysis.

* All comedy is very much of its time. We can't place ourselves back in that time and know how they felt.
* It's also worth noting that surprise is crucial to humor. This sketch is in the water now. You won't be surprised about anything about it at this point.

The classic "why did the chicken cross the road joke" is in fact a good joke. It's a nice turn. You state the obvious. It's just that you've understood it since you were 5 years old. You can't feel it any more. But it's still a good joke.

Love Cowen. He can break down a Beatles song like no one else. But stay out of comedy, my man. Not your metier. I know you love your girl Liz, but — let it go.
